strings.name: Ranil Wickremesinghe
strings.role: Former Sri Lankan president and six-time prime minister; UNP politician
strings.summary: Ranil Wickremesinghe is a Sri Lankan United National Party politician who entered Parliament in 1977, served as prime minister on six occasions and was president from 2022 to 2024. His career spans peace negotiations, coalition politics, the 2018 constitutional crisis and stabilisation policies following the 2022 economic crisis. His government pursued international financing and fiscal reform, but economic recovery, improvements in living standards and policy costs require separate assessment. Investigations into public spending after he left office must also be distinguished from criminal conviction.
strings.coverageNote: Information checked through 18 November 2026. The 2022 Gazette establishes his assumption of the presidency, and his successor’s 2024 proclamation clarifies the transition. Financing arrangements are distinguished from actual disbursements. Reporting of the 11 November court appearance supports recent activity; adjournment is neither a conviction nor an acquittal.
strings.influence.rationale: As a repeated prime minister and later president, he played a role in the economic crisis, debt restructuring and coordination within national politics.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birth and legal education
strings.facts.f1.value: Born on 24 March 1949. Parliamentary records list an LLB and professional legal qualifications, and describe legal education and student politics in Colombo. Legal qualification or honorary titles are not presented as a research doctorate.
strings.facts.f2.label: Repeated appointments and interruptions
strings.facts.f2.value: His premierships fell in 1993–1994, 2001–2004, separate periods from 2015 onward and 2022, rather than one continuous administration. After losing his seat in 2020, he returned to Parliament through the National List in 2021. The title MP on older records does not establish parliamentary membership in 2026.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Economic recovery and household living standards
strings.highlights.h1.text: In its 6 October 2026 assessment, the World Bank said Sri Lanka’s overall economy had regained pre-crisis levels, while household incomes and labour-market outcomes still lagged. This national assessment spans different administrations; the changes cannot all be credited to him personally, and it does not mean he remained president.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Public-funds investigation after leaving office
strings.highlights.h2.text: He was arrested in August 2025 over alleged misuse of public funds during his presidency. A report dated 11 November 2026 records his court appearance with the former presidential secretary and adjournment to 9 December for the Attorney General’s advice. Investigation, detention and adjournment are not final conviction; the December date remained a future arrangement.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Presidential transition
strings.timeline.t1.text: Anura Kumara Dissanayake took the presidential oath, marking the transition from Wickremesinghe’s presidency. The successor’s Gazette separately states that he was declared elected on 22 September and that his term commenced that day. Election results, commencement of the term and the oath therefore have distinct dates.
strings.timeline.t2.title: IMF approves an Extended Fund Facility arrangement
strings.timeline.t2.text: During his presidency, the IMF Executive Board approved a 48-month arrangement worth SDR 2.286 billion, then about US$3 billion, allowing an immediate disbursement of approximately US$333 million. The full allocation was not paid on that day; debt sustainability, fiscal reform and protection of vulnerable groups remained implementation tasks.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Assumes the presidency following a parliamentary election
strings.timeline.t3.text: After serving as acting president, he received 134 parliamentary votes on 20 July and assumed office under the Gazette on 21 July, to complete the term left unfinished by Gotabaya Rajapaksa’s resignation. This was a parliamentary election, not a direct popular vote granting a new full term.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Returns as prime minister during the economic crisis
strings.timeline.t4.text: Following Mahinda Rajapaksa’s resignation, he was appointed prime minister for the sixth time. From 25 May he also held the Finance, Economic Stabilisation and National Policies portfolio. This appointment is separate from his subsequent acting presidency and election as president.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Reappointed prime minister after the constitutional crisis
strings.timeline.t5.text: He was sworn in again after President Sirisena replaced him with Mahinda Rajapaksa in October, triggering a political impasse. Parliamentary votes and court proceedings formed the backdrop; the different judicial processes are not conflated into a single personal criminal judgment.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Government–LTTE ceasefire takes effect
strings.timeline.t6.text: Norway’s foreign minister announced on 22 February that the ceasefire document signed by Wickremesinghe for the government and by the LTTE leader had been deposited with Norway. It entered into force at midnight at the start of 23 February. The arrangement aimed to enable negotiations; it did not establish permanent peace at that time.
strings.timeline.t7.title: First appointment as prime minister
strings.timeline.t7.text: He became prime minister after President Premadasa’s assassination and Wijetunga’s succession to the presidency. His first premiership lasted until 19 August 1994. Periods in government and opposition followed; this early premiership is distinct from his later presidential term.
strings.timeline.t8.title: First elected to Parliament
strings.timeline.t8.text: He entered Parliament for the United National Party and held early government posts including deputy foreign minister and portfolios in youth affairs and education, before advancing to senior political leadership. Deputy foreign minister should not be described as foreign minister.
